Total Chess Pilot 2026 Day 1: Magnus plays the Dutch against the Dutch no.1 Top total chess Total Chess Pilot 2026 Day 3: 15 years later, Magnus' world no.1 spot in Danger
 Sagar Shah November 14, 2026 · 11 min read Magnus Carlsen has been the world no.1 since July 2011. After the third day of the Total Chess Pilot group stage in Budapest, Fabiano Caruana is just 7.2 points behind him on the live rating list. Fabi beat Vincent Keymer and is on 2800.0, while Magnus lost to Haik Martirosyan and dropped to 2807.2. Arjun Erigaisi beat Wesley So in a game full of twists, R. Vaishali sacrificed one piece after another to beat Bibisara Assaubayeva, and R. Praggnanandhaa drew both his games against Vladislav Artemiev.

Haik had dreamt of this game since he was a child | Photo: Maria Emelianova/Total Chess Each day of the group stage, players play two Fast Classic games (45 minutes plus 30 seconds a move) against the same opponent, with colours reversed. A win is 3 points, a draw 1. On the 13th of November, 10 of the 24 games were decisive.
 The fight for world no.1
 Magnus Carlsen has been the world no.1 since July 2011. Fifteen years at the top without a break. In Budapest that run is suddenly in danger.
 Magnus came into the Total Chess Pilot rated 2823, 40 points ahead of Fabiano Caruana (2783). After three days of the group stage the gap is just 7.2 points on the live rating list. Magnus has drawn five games and lost one, to Haik Martirosyan, and he has dropped 15.8 points to 2807.2. Fabi has won four games and drawn two, and he has gained 17 points to reach exactly 2800.0.
 Fabiano Caruana against Vincent Keymer. The win with Black took him to 2800 on the live list | Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess On the third day Fabi beat Vincent Keymer with the black pieces. He took over in the endgame and converted his advantage in 57 moves. Had he won the second game as well, he could have become the world no.1 right there. Keymer held him to a draw in 72 moves.
 The closest these two had been before was around their World Championship match in 2018, when the gap was about three points.
 Fabi has been the world no.2 for six years. Is this the moment he finally goes past Magnus? | Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess On the 14th of November Fabi plays Le Quang Liem, the only player anywhere near him in Group B, while Magnus faces Shakhriyar Mamedyarov. The world no.1 spot could change hands any day now.
 Haik Martirosyan's win over Magnus played a big part in all this. We brought you the news of that win in a short report, Haik Martirosyan defeats Magnus Carlsen for the first time at Total Chess Pilot 2026 . Here is the full story.
 Will there be a new World no.1? Our video on the race between Magnus and Fabi Martirosyan beats Magnus
 Magnus answered 1.e4 with the Sicilian Najdorf. Haik went for a quiet set-up with g3 and Bg2, and the game was balanced for a long time. Then came this moment.
 Martirosyan vs Carlsen, game one. Magnus has just recaptured on d5 with his pawn. The position is about equal, but now there is play for both sides After the game Haik explained: "after exd5 it was three results game and he was low on time and I started to play with his king and it worked perfect." In a relatively equal position Haik kept playing for a win, while Magnus was down to about a minute on his clock from move 27 onwards.
 Magnus has just played 36...Qb3, with 46 seconds left on his clock. White to move 36...Qb3 was the mistake. Haik brought his last rook into the attack with 37.Re1!, and the black king came under fire: 37...Qf7 38.Qc8+ Kh7 39.Re8 Qd5 40.Rh8+ Kg6 41.Qg4+.
 The final position. After 41...Bg5 42.h5+ it is mate soon. Magnus resigned 
 Haik Martirosyan has now won three of his six games, and leads Group C | Photo: Maria Emelianova/Total Chess 
 Four draws and then a loss: the Fast Classic has not been kind to Magnus so far | Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess Haik had dreamt of this game since he was a child. "It's very special moment for me. It will be hard to forget in this moment but I have to because I have second game," he told in the interviews. And about his approach: "the strategy was just to play good chess. Try to play good chess because okay if you do some mistakes you will take it immediately."
 The second game, with Magnus playing White, was drawn in 34 moves by repetition. Haik is on 10 points and leads Group C. Magnus is fifth with 5 points, and with two days to go he is far from the top.
 Magnus and Haik shake hands in the second game. A draw was enough for Haik to keep the lead | Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess After winning, Haik came on the ChessBase India live stream along with his fiancee. "Amazing day. I will remember this day in my life," he said. The secret was not to think about the opponent: "I was only thinking to play good chess... because if I all the time think that I'm playing Magnus it can be very bad for me."
 His fiancee is studying medicine, and she plays bullet on Chess.com! "She's also supporting me a lot during the tournament," Haik said. "I just need to just play my games." Watch Haik on our stream from 5:27:05 .
 The joy of beating your idol: Haik Martirosyan on his first ever classical game against Magnus Carlsen Arjun beats Wesley So
 Arjun took his chance when it came, and he is now on 9 points in Group D | Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess Arjun Erigaisi had the black pieces against Wesley So in the first game, and it was a tense battle. Wesley won an exchange on move 26.
 So vs Arjun Erigaisi, game one. 26.Bxe8: Wesley is an exchange up, but because of White's weak king, the position is balanced. Arjun had some chances, but then Wesley struck back.
 Arjun has just played 43...Re8. White to move: can you find the blow? 44.Rxh6+!! If 44...gxh6, then 45.Qf6+ and the white queen goes after the black king. Arjun played 44...Kg8, and now Wesley needed to finish it off.
 White to move. 45.Qg5! would have kept a winning attack. Wesley had eight seconds on his clock Instead of finishing it off, he faltered with 45.Qd6. Arjun defended, the game went into a long series of queen checks, and the position was equal. Then came the last mistake.
 After 53.Qg6 Arjun played 53...Be2! The rook on f3 is attacked, and if it moves, Qh1 is mate. Wesley was losing a rook or getting mated, and he resigned 
 Arjun and Wesley in the second game, a quick draw in 13 moves | Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess The second game was a quick draw. Quite uncharacteristic of Arjun. But maybe he just wanted a quiet day after all the action that happened in game 1. Arjun is on 9 points, level with Hans Niemann and three behind Maxime Vachier-Lagrave, whom he plays next.
 Arjun Erigaisi faces MVL, the leader of Group D, on the fourth day | Photo: Tor Nilssen/Total Chess 
 Wesley So is still looking for his first win in the Fast Classic | Photo: Tor Nilssen/Total Chess Vaishali's sacrifices
 Vaishali lost the first game against Bibisara Assaubayeva. The position was level for a long time, but with seconds on her clock she went wrong around move 39, and Bibisara won in 46 moves.
 Bibisara Assaubayeva won the first game, her second win of the group stage | Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess In the second game Vaishali played an incredible game. She got a big advantage out of the opening with her pawn on e6 stuck deep in Black's camp, and then she started sacrificing.
 Vaishali vs Assaubayeva, game two. White to move. Vaishali's rook is on e5 and the black king is short of defenders 28.Rxf5! A whole rook. After 28...gxf5 29.Nxf5 the knight jumped into d6 next, and Vaishali gave that up too.
 Bibisara has just taken the knight on d6. White to move: what would you play? 32.Re5!! The last rook comes in. If 32...Qc7, then 33.Rg5+ and it is mate in a few moves. Bibisara took it, 32...Qxe5 33.Qxe5, and Vaishali's queen and bishop were too much for the black king.
 35.Be3, and Bibisara resigned. The pawn on e6 and White's queen and bishop decide the game 
 Vaishali showed her attacking class in game 2 | Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess 
 Her first win of the Fast Classic, and what a way to get it | Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess This was Vaishali's first win of the Fast Classic. She is on 4 points.
 Pragg survives against Artemiev
 Pragg drew both his games against Vladislav Artemiev. The first one was intense and lasted 89 moves. Pragg was down to seconds on his clock, and at one point he was in real trouble.
 Praggnanandhaa vs Artemiev, game one. Pragg has just played 36.Bg3 with 32 seconds on his clock. Black to move Here 36...g6! would have won material for Black. The pawn on f5 is pinned. While this is very clear that Black is winning, once you see the move, it often is very tricky when you are under extreme time pressure, to change the character of the game in this fashion. Artemiev played 36...Rc8, Pragg got back into the game, and he survived somehow to make a draw. The second game was drawn by repetition in 19 moves.
 Two draws against Artemiev. Pragg is still looking for his first win in Budapest | Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess 
 Pragg was in trouble in the first game, but he held on | Photo: Michal Walusza/Total Chess The ChessBase India live stream of the day: Vaishali vs Bibisara, Pragg vs Artemiev, Arjun vs So The four groups after day three
 A win is 3 points, a draw is 1. If two players are level, the one who finished higher in the Blitz Swiss is ahead. Every group winner goes to Knockout 1, every runner-up to Knockout 2, and so on.

 Arjun against MVL is the big one for India: a win in that mini-match could put Arjun right in the race for the top of Group D. Firouzja meets Duda, Caruana meets Le Quang Liem, and Martirosyan defends his lead against Nepomniachtchi.
 The first game begins at 7.30 p.m. IST and the second at 11 p.m. IST. You can follow the games live on chessbase.in/live , with commentary on the ChessBase India YouTube channel .
